report_name: Maersk Confirms Breach; WhiteArmor Ransomware Demands $5M Ransom

threat_actors.name: WhiteArmor
threat_actors.description: A newly emerged ransomware group that claimed responsibility for the data breach at Maersk's subsidiary, LF Logistics. The group is conducting a double-extortion attack, demanding a $5 million ransom and threatening to release 100GB of stolen data.
threat_actors.goals: Extort a $5 million ransom from Maersk by threatening to release 100GB of stolen sensitive data.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor gained initial access by likely exploiting a vulnerability in the external-facing legacy OCF/LF Logistics platform.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The theft of plaintext passwords, including 33 SUPER_ADMIN accounts, allowed the threat actor to use valid accounts for access within the compromised legacy system.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor exfiltrated 100GB of sensitive data, likely to cloud storage, as part of the double-extortion attack.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The attack is part of a double-extortion strategy typical of ransomware groups, involving the threat of data encryption for impact, although encryption of Maersk's systems was not explicitly confirmed in the report.

malware.name: WhiteArmor Ransomware
malware.description: The malware associated with the WhiteArmor group, used in a double-extortion attack against Maersk. It is used to exfiltrate data and threaten encryption for impact to demand a ransom.

identities.name: Maersk
identities.description: A global shipping and logistics company that confirmed a data breach in a legacy IT system from its subsidiary, LF Logistics. The company is the target of a $5 million ransom demand.

identities.name: LF Logistics
identities.description: A logistics company acquired by Maersk in 2022 whose legacy IT system (OCF/LF Logistics platform) was the entry point for the data breach.

infrastructure.name: OCF/LF Logistics platform
infrastructure.description: A legacy IT system belonging to LF Logistics that was compromised by the WhiteArmor group to gain initial access and exfiltrate data.

indicators.name: Suspicious Data Archival Tool Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Data Archival Tool Execution
id: 2b8a1c3d-f4e5-4b6a-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of common data archival utilities often used by threat actors for data staging and compression before exfiltration.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/maersk-confirms-data-breach-as-whitearmor-ransomware-demands-5-million/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-12
tags:
  - attack.t1560.001
  - attack.collection
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\7z.exe'
      - '\rclone.exe'
      - '\winrar.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use by administrators or software deployment tools.
level: medium
indicators.description: Detects the execution of common data archival utilities (7z.exe, rclone.exe, winrar.exe) which are often used by threat actors to stage data for exfiltration.

indicators.name: Internal Reconnaissance Command Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Internal Reconnaissance Command Execution
id: 9d8c7b6a-5f4e-4d3c-2b1a-0e9f8d7c6b5a
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of common reconnaissance commands often run by attackers after gaining initial access to understand the network environment.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/maersk-confirms-data-breach-as-whitearmor-ransomware-demands-5-million/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-12
tags:
  - attack.t1087
  - attack.t1033
  - attack.discovery
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
      - '\nltest.exe'
  filter_net_time:
    CommandLine|contains: ' time'
  condition: selection and not filter_net_time
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity or scripts.
level: low
indicators.description: Detects the execution of common reconnaissance commands (net user, whoami, nltest) used to discover information about the local system and domain.

indicators.name: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4d3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of encoded commands in PowerShell, a technique frequently used by attackers to obfuscate their actions.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/maersk-confirms-data-breach-as-whitearmor-ransomware-demands-5-million/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-12
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1027
  - attack.execution
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -enc '
      - ' -encodedcommand '
      - ' -e '
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate scripts that use encoded commands for complex arguments.
level: high
indicators.description: Detects the execution of PowerShell with encoded commands, a common technique for obfuscating malicious scripts.
